01 — The shape of your reach

One post is a third of everything

Your reach isn't spread evenly — it's hit-driven. A single video ("i don't think donald is going to like my new single…") pulled 224K, which is 35.8% of all the views across these 55 posts. Your top 10 hold 75.7%. The gap between your average (11.4K) and your median (3.3K) says the same thing: most posts land modestly, and a few break the roof.

That's not a flaw — it's the game on TikTok. It means the goal isn't a higher floor, it's more swings at the ceiling. Everything below is about which swings connect.

02 — The reach engine

Your angle matters more than your song

Grouping every post by the angle of its hook, one pattern dominates: the closer a post gets to a topical, comment-baiting claim, the higher it flies. Bars in orange beat your 11.4K average; grey falls below it.

The "where are you from?" geo-bait tops the list — all three uses landed (median 34K, higher than the mean). The underdog / small-artist angle, your most-used at 11 posts, sits dead last at 4.3K. You lean on it most and it pays least.

03 — Five rules your data actually proves

How you write the line

Same account, same music — the construction of the sentence swings reach by multiples. These five hold up across the set.

04 — Hashtags, ranked by what they returned

Topical tags out-pull music tags

Average views for every hashtag you've used at least three times. The news-cycle tags (#epsteinfiles, #trump, #iran) and #singersongwriter beat your average; the generic music tags you reach for by habit — #newmusic, #indiemusic, #nzmusic — quietly sit below it.

Read this carefully: a hashtag doesn't cause views — the topical tags ride on the topical posts that were always going to travel. The tag is a marker of the angle, not a magic word. Don't bolt #epsteinfiles onto a love song.

05 — What quietly kills reach

Stop feeding these

6.2K
"POV:" overlays. Your 11 POV-opener posts average 6.2K — below your baseline. The format is overused and underperforming; your real winners open first-person and plain ("i'm convinced…", "i don't think…"), not as a staged POV.
3.2K
Reply-to-comment videos. Great for community, weak for reach — they cluster near the bottom. Use them to reward fans, never as your push for a new song.
2.7K
Lyric / karaoke videos with no spoken hook. Lowest format in the set. If you post one, still stamp a text hook over the first second before the lyrics roll.
4.2K
Sentence-case, "announcement" phrasing. Hooks that start with a capital and read like marketing average 4.2K vs 19.1K for your lowercase, confessional lines. The polish is the problem.

06 — The synthesis

Build your next hook

Every winning element above, stacked into one repeatable recipe. Not every post can be political — but every post can borrow the construction.

  1. Lead first-person and lowercase."i'm convinced…", "i don't think…", "pretty sure i've just…". The raw voice out-pulls the capitalised pitch 4-to-1.
  2. Make a claim, not an announcement.A suppression angle ("tiktok keeps pulling this down") or a geo-claim ("only showing my music to NZ") beats "out now" every time.
  3. End on a question."where are you from?" — a comment-bait question nearly doubles average views and lifts the median 5×.
  4. Keep it 7–12 words.Your sharpest bucket. Long enough to carry the claim, short enough to read in a second.
  5. Tag the angle, not the genre.Topical + #singersongwriter over a pile of generic music tags.
i'm convinced tiktok keeps burying this song about [topic]. where are you listening from?
caption: the reason i wrote it → #singersongwriter #theillcollective #[topical]

07 — Method & honest caveats

Read this before you over-trust it

Sample: your 55 posts that cleared 1,000 views (the copy-bible set), scored on view count, hook, and caption. No dates or engagement were available, so this can't yet answer "best this week" or engagement rate — a TikTok Studio export unlocks both. Small groups (censorship framing n=5, geo-bait n=3) show the ceiling clearly but are thin — treat them as strong priors to test, not laws. And view count is also moved by posting time, the audio you used, and the algorithm's mood that day, none of which are in this data. The right use of this page is a hypothesis list: keep making the confessional, topical, question-ended swings, and watch whether the pattern holds as the sample grows.
